name: Fire
summary: Fire 0.6.0: a design system for developer, agent and AI products, in its default look (the Ember palette, Geist and Geist Mono). Plain HTML and CSS are the contract: classes fd-*, variants and states through data-* and ARIA, tokens --fd-*. Light and dark values are exact; this content is generated from contract/fire-contract.json and contract/catalog.json, so edit the theme record (facet/theme.json), not these tokens.

muted.$description: Fire --fd-text-3 (an alpha token) laid over --fd-bg, so the value is opaque.

on-primary.$description: Fire --fd-accent-contrast: the label on the accent fill.

accent.$description: Fire has one accent, so this repeats primary; Facet may set another.

link.$description: Fire --fd-accent-text: accent text on the page, darkened to pass 4.5:1.

touch.$description: The default control on a coarse pointer (Fire grows --fd-control-md to 40px there).

motion.notes: Fire collapses every duration through one token: under prefers-reduced-motion it sets --fd-motion to 0 and --fd-press-scale to 1, and each duration is the token times --fd-motion, so nothing animates. Looping spinners and shimmers stop with it.

dont: The action is a link to another page, or sits inside a sentence. The text button (fd-btn-text)…
Several related actions belong together as one control. The button group (fd-btn-group), part of…

components.purpose: A native table with a scrolling wrapper, sortable headers, optional row selection with a bulk bar, expandable and clickable rows, sticky headers, and…
do: People compare the same fields across many records: logs, keys, invoices, runs.
Rows need sorting, selection, bulk actions or an actions cell.
dont: Records are few and each needs a title, a description and several controls. Use List.
The data is a handful of label and value pairs for one record. Use Kv.

voice.tone: Plain, specific, direct, calm and honest. The screen is the explanation and words fill only the gaps. Second person, active voice, present tense. Developers think in endpoints, keys, credits and requests: use those words, with identifiers in mono. No exclamation marks, no "Oops", no padding "please" or "sorry".
do: Name tasks by what the person does and places by what they are: "Scrape a page", "API keys".
Give every button a verb or a verb and its object ("Create key", "Export CSV"); the primary button in a dialog repeats the dialog title's verb.
Replace adjectives with facts: numbers, names, dates ("about 2 seconds", "Nov 23", "1,520 credits").
Say each thing once: if the title says "API keys", the description does not begin "API keys are".
Write errors as what happened, then what to do: "Couldn't reach docs.example.com. Check the URL, or try again in a minute."
Write empty states as a short title, one sentence saying what will appear, and one action.
Use sentence case; titles, labels and buttons have no full stop, descriptions and errors do.
Set identifiers (keys, IDs, paths, endpoints, file names) in mono and never reword them.
Confirm only what cannot be undone or costs money; otherwise act and offer Undo.
Name one thing one way across the interface, the docs and the API (Create, Add, Remove, Delete, Revoke).
dont: Do not write "OK", "Submit", "Yes", "Click here" or a bare "Continue" on a button.
Do not use simply, just, easily, quickly, successfully, basically, actually or very.
Do not restate the title, the label or the value in a description or hint.
Do not blame the person ("You entered an invalid URL") or show a raw status code as the whole error.
Do not put anything a person must read to finish the task in a tooltip.
Do not list the allowed answers in a hint under a text box: the control is wrong, use a select, segmented control or switch.
Do not describe emptiness ("There is nothing here") or apologise in an empty state.
Do not stack callouts: one that interrupts is useful, three mean none matter.
Do not invent product names for ordinary things.
